resources.string: Confirm your screen lock to issue licenses
This device holds a license-signing key. Confirm your fingerprint, face, or device PIN to continue.

The signing key is protected by the Android Keystore and can only be used within a short window after you unlock the device. Set a screen lock (PIN, pattern, or password) first — biometrics alone in Settings > Security are not enough.
Open the verifier screen — the exact same screen license holders see (same offline verification, same public key).

This build can sign licenses completely offline, on this device.

What that means honestly:
• The Ed25519 seed is stored wrapped by the Android Keystore and only unwrapped within 60 seconds of a successful unlock.
• Anyone with this device AND its unlock can issue licenses; a compromised OS could observe a signing operation.
• Licenses are not revocable once issued — prefer short validity windows. The History tab is only a local ledger, not a revocation list.
• This app has no network permission at all: nothing is ever uploaded, checked online, or synchronized.
• Raising the bar is not making it unbreakable. A rooted, fully compromised device defeats any on-device scheme.

Wipe the signing key from this device?

The wrapped seed and its metadata are deleted. Issued licenses stay valid; the history is kept. Without a backup the key is gone — you will not be able to issue licenses that verify with the same public key.
The passphrase protects the backup file (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM). It is never stored and cannot be recovered — losing it means losing the backup.

Buyer apps that embed a different key still accept your licenses after they pair with this code once: send it together with the license (any channel — it only carries the PUBLIC key, so it can never enable forgery). In the buyer app: license screen → “Pair reseller key” → paste.
